subject: Request: Adjusted completion tolerance for nightly bulk jobs and idempotency guidance
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@medsys.io>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Nightly bulk SLA — completion window flexibility & retries

Diego / Lauren,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. One operational constraint we need to surface as we move into contract: our nightly inference pipeline processes roughly 9–12M records in a single window starting ~02:00 local (PST). Historically it has completed within ~5–6 hours but there are seasonal spikes that push long-tail completion to 7–9 hours.

Given the volume and the downstream billing/ETL cutover at 10:00, our ops team is asking whether Redwood can accept a completion-window SLA of 8 hours for these nightly bulk jobs (vs. the 6-hour standard in the hosted SLA). We also need explicit guidance on safe retry behavior and whether idempotency tokens can guarantee no double-processing for replays or backfills.

Attached is a small profile of job size / distribution (medsys_nightly_profile.csv). Can you outline what scope of exception we could agree to (time window, retry attempts, credits) and what changes would be needed on our side (idempotency token header, request dedupe key, etc.)? We want to avoid building an ad-hoc orchestration loop if Redwood can handle safe retries reliably.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min SRE pairing call.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Data Ops, MedSys Health
elena.park@medsys.io
+1 415-555-0192

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Nightly bulk SLA — completion window flexibility & retries (triage)

Folks — forwarding Elena's note and profile. High level ask: medsys is requesting an 8-hour completion window for large nightly jobs and wants firm guidance on retries/idempotency so they can rely on our platform rather than building orchestration themselves.

Questions for quick triage:
- Operational: what are the realistic completion SLOs for a 10M job on our Dedicated hosts vs Hosted?
- Retry semantics: can we support idempotency token semantics that guarantee no duplicate outputs even with multiple replay attempts?
- Credits/financials: what credit level do we offer if long-tail goes beyond agreed window? (Sales side)
- Monitoring: what alerts/proofs can we provide back to MedSys for acceptance testing?

Please reply with a recommended exception proposal we can present — try to be concrete (hours, number of retries, backstop behavior). Customer asked for a short summary by EOD tomorrow so they can align procurement.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Manager, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nightly bulk SLA — completion window flexibility & retries (technical proposal)

Diego / team,

Quick technical proposal based on the job profile:
- Completion window: propose a 7.5-hour contractual window (start at job ingestion timestamp). Rationale: median completion is ~5.5h; 95th percentile ~7h; 8h is conservative but pushes cost/contingency. 7.5h gives a measurable buffer while limiting exposure.
- Retry policy: allow up to 3 safe retries per job segment (segment = 100k-record shard) with exponential backoff (30s, 2m, 8m). Retries beyond that trigger automated cutover to a background finalization workflow tracked separately (see below).
- Idempotency: require an idempotency_key header per job request. We will guarantee exactly-once semantics at the shard granularity if idempotency_key + shard_id are provided. Without it we can only provide at-least-once.
- Safe-retry design: Redwood will maintain a per-customer KV of seen idempotency tokens for 14 days (configurable). Replays with the same token will be deduped before scoring. This uses ~0.3GB per 100k tokens/day overhead for our KV store (ballpark).
- Monitoring & proof: we can provide a per-job run report (start, per-shard retries, final status, tail-latency) exported to S3 or pushed to their SRE webhook. We can also provide a daily digest and a Grafana dashboard link for live diagnostics.
- Credits: suggest a tiered credit: 25% credit on token usage for any nightly job finishing between 7.5 and 9 hours; 50% credit if >9 hours and we cannot present post-mortem within 72 hours. (Sales, legal to firm up.)

I've attached a short "safe-retry" spec that outlines the idempotency headers and shard dedupe semantics. We should confirm storage retention and cost assumptions with infra (Marcus).

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

—— Attachment: redwood_safe-retry-spec.pdf (PDF, 46KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.io>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nightly bulk SLA — completion window flexibility & retries (proposal)

Elena — thanks for the profile and for outlining the constraint. Based on our internal review, Redwood can offer the following exception package for MedSys' nightly bulk jobs:

Summary of proposed exception (formal):
- Completion window: 7.5 hours from job ingestion timestamp for nightly bulk jobs (defined as ingest >5M records).
- Retry & idempotency: customer must send idempotency_key and shard_id per job segment. Redwood will dedupe on idempotency_key+shard_id and supports up to 3 retry attempts with the exponential backoff described by our SRE team (30s, 2m, 8m).
- Credits: 25% service credit on billable token usage for jobs finishing in (7.5h, 9h]; 50% credit for jobs finishing >9h pending post-mortem.
- Guardrails & monitoring: Redwood will provide a per-job report (S3 export or webhook) and a shared Grafana dashboard. We will also run a 1-week acceptance window after go-live to tune shard sizing and backoff parameters.
- Duration & review: this exception will be valid for 6 months from go-live and then reviewed for renewal.

Next steps we propose:
1) If acceptable, elect one of the following sign-off options: a) confirm in HubSpot (link below) b) sign the attached one-page amendment via DocuSign.
2) Kickoff SRE pairing session to validate idempotency headers (we recommend a single 60-min session).
3) Provide PO to enable Dedicated capacity reservation if you choose reserved hosts.

I've copied Diego and Rishi for technical and contractual follow-through. Attaching the safe-retry spec and a one-page amendment for signature.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

—— Attachments: redwood_safe-retry-spec.pdf (PDF, 46KB); amendment_nightly_exception_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
